book.title: Creativity: Flow and the Psychology of Discovery and Invention
book.author: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi

confidence_note: Source is thin. The five-step list is cited to the book in secondary sources (p. 79 per one blog); page not read. Old four stages and Newton, Archimedes and Kekule examples dropped as unconfirmed. No named case, so the story stays near the length floor.
facts: The book rests on in-depth interviews with about 91 exceptional individuals from many fields (one catalogue says nearly one hundred).
Csikszentmihalyi says the creative process normally takes five steps.
Preparation: becoming immersed in a set of problematic issues.
Incubation: ideas churn around below the threshold of consciousness.
Insight: the moment when the pieces of the puzzle fall together.
Evaluation: deciding whether the insight is worth pursuing.
Elaboration: the longest and hardest part of the process.
He warns that the steps are more recursive than linear.
Caveat: reports of incubation come from creators looking back, sometimes years later, and a 2016 review calls their reliability questionable.

Graham Wallas drew on Poincare's 1910 account of mathematical creation and named the stage of unconscious work 'incubation'; Poincare's own report concerned events nearly thirty years earlier (editorial context from a 2016 review).
scene_details: the aha moment placed third in a list of five
elaboration named as the longest step
tension: The moment everyone remembers is the third of five steps, and not the longest.
opening_idea: Open on the count: five steps, and the flash of insight is only the third.

lessons.idea: Count elaboration as part of the idea
lessons.anchor: insight as step three of five and elaboration as the longest; Everyday: a home cook who invents a soup in a flash and then adjusts salt and timing for weeks

reflect_final: Think of an idea of yours that stalled after the first spark. Which step were you in, and what did it still need?

use_cases.situation: A colleague is discouraged that their idea needs more work
use_cases.move: Csikszentmihalyi puts the aha at step three of five and elaboration last and longest. Which step are we in now?

use_cases.situation: The team wants quick results from a brainstorm
use_cases.move: Insight is one of five steps. Let's agree on how we will evaluate it before we start building.

use_cases.situation: You drop ideas once the excitement fades
use_cases.move: The spark is step three. I will write down what elaboration would still ask of me before I give up.

pocket_idea: The aha is step three of five. If an idea feels stalled, name which step it is in.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: The aha moment is only step three of five in Csikszentmihalyi's account of how creativity works.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Csikszentmihalyi says the creative process normally takes five steps: preparation, incubation, insight, evaluation and elaboration. The aha is third. Elaboration is the longest and hardest. He warns the steps loop more than they line up, and a later review notes that creators' memories of incubation may not be reliable.
